about: Château Pontet-Canet takes its name from Jean-François de Pontet, an 18th-century royal governor of the Médoc, and from the Canet lands his descendants added. It was ranked a Fifth Growth in 1855. The Cruse merchant family owned it for 110 years, and in 1975 the Cognac merchant Guy Tesseron bought it. His son Alfred has run it since 1994, and Justine Tesseron now leads it with him. The 81 hectares of vines lie almost in one piece, next to Mouton Rothschild.

Pontet-Canet is one of Bordeaux’s most radical estates. It began biodynamic trials in 2004 and in 2010 became the first major Médoc château certified organic. It also holds Biodyvin biodynamic certification, and Breton horses plough much of the vineyard. The 2016 was picked from 28 September to 12 October, Merlot first and Cabernet Sauvignon from 4 October. It was aged about 16 months, partly in French oak and partly in concrete amphorae made for the estate, some of them from its own soil.

2016 was a classic, cool-finishing Médoc vintage, and Pontet-Canet’s 2016 is one of its finest wines. The estate describes a deep colour and a powerful, pure nose, with a dense, full and refreshing palate and succulent, precise tannins. Lisa Perrotti-Brown, writing for Wine Advocate, gave it 98 points and noted plum preserves, spice and cassis, a velvety texture and a long mineral finish.
facts: 65% Cabernet Sauvignon, 30% Merlot, 3% Cabernet Franc, 2% Petit Verdot
About 16 months in French oak (about half new) and concrete amphorae
